title: Polynomial-Time Conditional Branching
statement: Let $p$ be a Boolean-valued test on finite Boolean words, and let $f,g$ be functions from finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words. If the function that outputs the single-bit word encoding $p(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, and both $f$ and $g$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function that returns $f(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ maps finite Boolean words to Booleans
$f,g$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
The single-bit function $x\mapsto[p(x)]$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: Let $p$ be a Boolean test whose single-bit indicator is polynomial-time computable, and let $f$ and $g$ be polynomial-time computable functions on binary strings. Then the function that returns $f(x)$ when $p(x)$ holds and $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
